A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RALA/RAVLT work, with readable text, equations, tables and figures. v1 ends with references; v4 includes Appendices A–C. The retained material and additions can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, detection, segmentation and ablation results for RALA/RAVLT in Section 4, together with empirical rank analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and adds a RAVLT-T/UperNet result and the weighting ablation in Appendix A, Table 10.

M1.justification: The proposed attention-score weighting, output modulation, kernel, positional encoding and RAVLT architectures remain unchanged in Equations 3–6 and Table 1. The learned-weight alternative in Appendix A is an ablation, not a revision of the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions retain ImageNet-1K, ImageNet-V2, ADE20K and the same classification, detection and segmentation task coverage. The additional experiments use existing coverage with another model configuration or weighting control.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in the existing benchmark tables and figures are retained. Appendix A, Table 10 adds a learned weighting vector as an explicit comparison method against RALA's attention-score weighting under DeiT-T.

E3.justification: v4 adds RAVLT-T to the existing UperNet 160K evaluation and a DeiT-T control using a learned 1×N weighting vector. Appendix C discloses settings for existing experiments without establishing changes to their previous training or preprocessing.

E4.justification: Appendix A adds an ablation testing attention-score weights against learned weights, restricted to classification because the learned vector has a fixed token count. The existing component, function-choice and layer-rank analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or comparable uncertainty estimates. The new results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 7 replaces missing RAVLT-T/UperNet entries with 44M parameters, 893G FLOPs and 49.3% mIoU. Table 10 adds learned-weight accuracy of 73.8%, versus the retained 75.1% attention-score result. Existing benchmark scores and the throughput and layer-rank curves otherwise remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Beyond v1's attention equations and matrix-product rank bound, v4 adds coefficient-based rank arguments in Appendix A, Equations 7–11, and a rank-one decomposition deriving the Hadamard-product rank bound in Appendix B, Equations 12–15. This substantially expands the formal justification offered for both augmentations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central claims: low output-feature rank explains linear attention's performance deficit, RALA addresses it through two augmentations, and RAVLT combines efficiency with strong vision performance. The headline 84.4% ImageNet result is unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix A adds an interpretation based on adaptive coefficient flexibility and identifies resolution limitations of fixed-length learned weights. Appendix B links function-choice insensitivity to Hadamard multiplication and makes an unconditional rank-enhancement claim that its upper bound does not establish.

D1.justification: Appendix C substantially expands reproducibility information: 300 classification epochs, Adam, learning-rate scheduling, warm-up, batch size, weight decay and augmentation settings, plus detection resizing and optimization details and segmentation input sizes. v1 mainly referred readers to prior training recipes.

R1.justification: v4 adds citations for RandAugment, CutMix, mixup and Vision Transformer with Sparse Scan Prior. Section 2 also softens the assertion that previous methods do not address low rank to the narrower observation that the problem persists.

P1.justification: The abstract and conclusion receive localized language edits, captions and cross-references are refined, and Appendices A–C provide additional organization. The main section sequence and most explanatory prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 6 is redrawn with numbered operations; Figure 3's legends and Figure 7's axis range are revised without changing their results. v4 also adds Table 10 and architecture Figure 9, with smaller table-header, caption and placement changes elsewhere.

improvement.justification: Appendix C improves reproducibility, Table 10 adds targeted evidence, and Figure 6 clarifies computation. However, Appendix A's coefficient factorization does not establish greater ability to obtain full-rank buffers, while Appendix B's upper bound cannot justify guaranteed rank enhancement. These new weaknesses concern the central mechanism, leaving the net quality effect of the documentation and empirical gains uncertain.
